THOUGHT: This 65‑year‑old woman has recurrent bilateral anterior chamber inflammation (iritis) over several months with keratic precipitates and anterior chamber cells and now symptomatic cystoid macular edema (CME) with subfoveal fluid in the right eye on OCT and angiographic leakage. Workup for systemic rheumatologic, infectious, and chest (sarcoid) causes was unrevealing. The history of long‑term anastrozole (aromatase inhibitor) therapy for breast cancer is important because aromatase inhibitors have been reported to cause inflammatory ocular reactions including uveitis and macular edema. The pattern—predominantly anterior inflammation with secondary CME, lack of peripheral vitreous or pars plana snowbanking (making pars planitis less likely), absence of characteristic birdshot fundus lesions or vitritis (making birdshot less likely), normal chest CT and labs (reducing likelihood of sarcoidosis or systemic vasculitis), and no high IOP or corneal necrosis to suggest herpetic/CMV disease—supports a drug‑induced or idiopathic chronic anterior uveitis with secondary CME as the leading possibilities. Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis can produce chronic low‑grade anterior inflammation and CME but is usually unilateral and has characteristic stellate KPs and heterochromia. Viral anterior uveitis (HSV/CMV/VZV) remains possible and would warrant aqueous PCR if suspected. Birdshot and other posterior uveitides are less likely given the exam and imaging findings. 

DIAGNOSIS:
1) Drug‑induced uveitis and secondary cystoid macular edema — most likely related to long‑term anastrozole therapy  
2) Chronic idiopathic anterior uveitis with secondary CME  
3) Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis (atypical/bilateral presentation)  
4) Viral anterior uveitis (HSV/CMV/VZV) with secondary CME  
5) Posterior uveitis (e.g., birdshot chorioretinopathy) presenting with bilateral CME
ground_truth: Anastrozole-associated uveitis with cystoid macular edema

Case Information:
A 65-year-old woman presented with blurry vision in her right eye for several months. Ocular history included 3 recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis occurring during 5 months, amblyopia in the left eye, and bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens. Patient had undergone left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior and had been on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years. Medical history and past medication use were otherwise unremarkable.

Physical Examination:
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS without improvement on pinhole testing. Intraocular pressures were normal. Right eye showed trace conjunctival injection without definite ciliary flush, 2+ fine keratic precipitates, and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber. Left eye had a few keratic precipitates. Dilated fundus examination revealed cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye and an epiretinal membrane in the left eye. No inflammation in the periphery was noted in either eye.

Diagnostic Tests:
- Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT):  Image Title: OCT Scans  Image Description: Right eye showed significant cystoid macular edema and subfoveal fluid. Left eye had a mild epiretinal membrane.- Fluorescein Angiography:  Image Title: Fundus Fluorescein Angiography  Image Description: Revealed cystoid macular edema with leakage in both right and left eyes.- Blood Tests: Tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders were within reference limits. Normal findings for tick-borne and bacterial diseases.- Imaging:  Computed tomography of the chest was unremarkable.
